newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan monopoly hands new blow to Vietnam refinery.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan monopoly hands new blow to Vietnam refinery.

text.p: Taiwan's state oil monopoly on Monday threw a new wrench into Vietnam's plans to build its first refinery, saying it was likely to leave an international consortium formed to build the $1.6 billion project.
"Chinese Petroleum reviewed the Vietnam refinery project and is likely to stop the plan due to its low investment return," a company official told Reuters by telephone.
That view resulted from the Vietnam's unwillingness to offer favorable treatment to the project, the official said.
Chinese Petroleum Corporation's (CPC) comment was the latest in a string of setbacks for Vietnamese sponsor Petrovietnam, which had denied as recently as February 13 that the consortium was wavering.
The state-run company has said it was not prepared to offer the concessions demanded by its foreign partners and it would build the refinery on its own if necessary.
Analysts have said Vietnam had neither the capital nor the technology and expertise to do it alone.
Under existing plans, CPC and Taiwan's China Investment Development Corp comprise 10 percent of the project's foreign consortium.
China Investment would only take part if Chinese Petroleum, which insists on a 15 percent return for investment, went ahead.
A CPC review projected a return rate at less than half of the target, the official said.

Other partners include Petrovietnam with a 30 percent stake, South Korea's LG Group with 27 percent, Stone & Webster with three percent, and Malaysia's Petronas and U.S. refiner Conoco split a 30 percent equally.
The $1.6 billion Dung Quat oil refinery, designed with a capacity of 6.5 million tonnes per year, is to be built in the central province of Quang Ngai.

In recent months, negotiations with the consortium have slowed, reportedly because of demands that Hanoi give price gaurantees for the refined petroleum, and over foreign partners' demands for access to Vietnam's consumer market.

The CPC official said Petronas and Conoco also were likely to withdraw their investment for the same reason, but LG Group and Stone & Webster had no plans to back out of what could be a lucrative construction project.
"LG and Stone Webster are likely to stay on the plan and are seeking the refinery project's construction contract," he said.
LG Group officials in Seoul confirmed that they had no plans to quit the project and would strive to win the contract to build the refinery.
The French oil firm Total SA withdrew from the refinery project in 1995, calling it economically unviable.
